First explore the data from Jin-2025 experiment

Mouse brain data from Xin Jin's lab \~ 2025 and downloaded from dropbox

Email: Ergan to Jin-Hong to Catherine:

```         
    Please check the following two links of the data available.
    Those data is shared in 2 batches by Seoyeon, where one is containing 10 perturbations and another one contains 48 perturbations.

    
    Both datasets have the aligned cell types and you can easily use sc.concat([data_1, data_2]) to combine them.
```

# Construct grna matrix

There are two ways we can construct tests. Suppose we have three perturbations targeting the same gene called guideA1, guideA2, and guideA3.

We can test for individual guides to genes: (guideA1 - gene) (guideA2 - gene) (guideA3 - gene)

Or we can combine them: \[guideA1 or guideA2 or guideA3\] - gene

I think these are usually combined. In our case, we would also want to separate the Non-Targeting perturbations in order to construct true Null tests.

We will create 2 grna matrices-

- grna: #cells x #targeted genes+1NT = 253,587 x 58 targeted genes +1NT- for cell i and gene target j, the (i,j)th element will be a 1 if the cell received any of the guides that targeted this gene
- grnaNT

Most targeted genes have 4 guides targeting this gene (all except Prpf6, which has 3). There are 399 Non-targeting guides.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| output: false
metadata_all$gene_target |> unique() |> length()
metadata_all$guide_call |> unique() |> length()
metadata_all |> select(guide_call, gene_target) |> distinct() |> arrange(gene_target, guide_call)

metadata_all |>  select(guide_call, gene_target) |> filter(gene_target == 'Non_target') 
metadata_all |> group_by(gene_target) |> summarize(n_guides = length(unique(guide_call)))
```

```{r}
# construct grna: perturbation assignment for combined perturbations 
grna = model.matrix(~gene_target-1, 
             data = metadata_all |> mutate(gene_target = relevel(gene_target, ref = 'Non_target')),
             check.names = FALSE)
colnames(grna) <- sub("^gene_target", "", colnames(grna))
grna = t(grna)                                               # feature x cell
grna = as(grna, 'dgRMatrix')                                 # convert to sparse matrix



# construct grnaNT: perturbation assignment for individual Non_target perturbations 
grnaNT = model.matrix(~guide_call-1 , 
             data = metadata_all,
             check.names = FALSE)
colnames(grnaNT) <- sub("^guide_call", "", colnames(grnaNT))
grnaNT = grnaNT[, grepl('Non_target', colnames(grnaNT))]     # subset only NT guides
grnaNT = t(grnaNT)                                           # feature x cell
grnaNT = as(grnaNT, 'dgRMatrix')                             # convert to sparse matrix


# some checks
assertthat::assert_that(all(row.names(grna) %in% metadata_all$gene_target), msg='grna matrix cols should match gene targets')
assertthat::assert_that(all(row.names(grnaNT) %in% metadata_all$guide_call), msg='grnaNT matrix cols should match guide calls')
```

The dimension of `grna` is `{r} dim(grna)`

The dimension of `grnanT` is `{r} dim(grnaNT)`

## Calculate gene deviance/importance (+ add TF and housekeep info)

Choose the top `params$NUM_IMPORTANT_GENES`=`{r} params$NUM_IMPORTANT_GENES` genes by the most important (the most deviant genes) from `scry::devianceFeatureSelection`

```{r}
# load if already saved
if(!params$RUN_EVEN_IF_SAVED & 'gene_dev.csv' %in% list.files(save_dir)) {
  gene_dev_df = read.csv(file = sprintf('%s/gene_dev.csv', save_dir)) 
} else {
  # subset the data because there are a lot of cells, CELL_SUBSET_SIZE = 25000 around this much, some rounding
  
  prop_10pert = jin2025_10pert$n_obs() / (jin2025_10pert$n_obs() + jin2025_48pert$n_obs()) # sample prop from each dataset
  
  # round(prop_10pert * params$CELL_SUBSET_SIZE)
  # jin2025_10pert$shape()
  # dim(jin2025_10pert$X) # 110968 19070- oh X is cell x gene
  # dim(jin2025_48pert$X)
  # jin2025_10pert$X[1:4, 1:5]
  
  
  
  counts_subset = rbind(jin2025_10pert$X[sample(jin2025_10pert$n_obs(), size = round(   prop_10pert  * params$CELL_SUBSET_SIZE), replace = FALSE), ],
                        jin2025_48pert$X[sample(jin2025_48pert$n_obs(), size = round((1-prop_10pert) * params$CELL_SUBSET_SIZE), replace = FALSE), ])
  counts_subset = t(counts_subset) # cell x gene
  # dim(counts_subset) # 19070 genes x # subsampled cells
  
  # Input should be: row = feature, col = cell
  gene_dev = scry::devianceFeatureSelection(object=counts_subset, fam='binomial') # < 1 min
  gene_dev_df = data.frame(gene_idx = 1:length(gene_dev), deviance=gene_dev)  |> 
                dplyr::arrange(desc(gene_dev)) |> dplyr::mutate(importance_rank = 1:n())  # add rank importance 
  gene_dev_df = gene_dev_df[names(gene_dev), ] |> tibble::rownames_to_column(var = 'gene_name') |> # reorder to original
                dplyr::mutate(is_grna_target = (gene_name %in%  gene_target_order)) # add T/F is a perturbation target
  
  
  # add columns: is transcription factor and is housekeeping gene
  gene_dev_df = gene_dev_df |> mutate(is_transcription_factor = (gene_name %in% TF_list),
                                      is_housekeeping = (gene_name %in% housekeepgenes) )
  
  # get (top X genes + grna target genes + housekeeping genes?) x (all cells)
  # (bc prev counts_subset used to calculate gene dev subset cells for performance)
  gene_dev_df = gene_dev_df |> mutate(is_normalized_gene = importance_rank <= params$NUM_IMPORTANT_GENES | is_grna_target | is_housekeeping) 
  

  write.csv(x = gene_dev_df, file = sprintf('%s/gene_dev.csv', save_dir), row.names = FALSE) # csv 
  rm(gene_dev, counts_subset, prop_10pert)
}
normalized_genes_names = gene_dev_df |> filter(is_normalized_gene) |> pull(gene_name) |> sort()
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| output: false

gene_dev_df |> filter(importance_rank <= params$NUM_IMPORTANT_GENES | is_grna_target | is_housekeeping) |> 
  arrange(desc(importance_rank)) |> pull(is_transcription_factor) |> table()

gene_dev_df |> filter(importance_rank <= params$NUM_IMPORTANT_GENES | is_grna_target | is_housekeeping) |> select(is_grna_target | is_housekeeping) |> table()
```

# PCA


```{r}
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| output: false
#| echo: true
# subsample size (same used in gene deviance calcs)
set.seed(12345)
subsample_cells = sample(ncol(gene_norm), size=params$CELL_SUBSET_SIZE, replace=FALSE) |> sort()
gene_norm_PCA = gene_norm[, subsample_cells] |> t()

# perform pca
pca_res = prcomp(x = gene_norm_PCA, rank.=100, retx = TRUE, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# construct NCs as the actual loadings: [all cells x valid genes] %*% [rotation of valid genes x PCs]
# NC_loadings = t(gene_norm) %*% pca_res$rotation
NC_loadings = scale(t(gene_norm), center=TRUE,scale=TRUE) %*% pca_res$rotation # should center/scale first oops, but they are linearlly corr so i don't think it matters much hopefully

# save
dir.create(sprintf('%s/pca/', save_dir), showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(NC_loadings, sprintf('%s/pca/NCloadings.rds', save_dir)) 


rm(subsample_cells, gene_norm_PCA)

```


```{r}
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| output: false
# test if data needs to be scaled and centered first
library(DelayedMatrixStats)
library(sparseMatrixStats)


subsample_cells
pca_mult_loadings = gene_norm_PCA %*% pca_res$rotation[, 1:2]


apply(gene_norm_PCA, CenterTitle)
pca_mult_loadings_centerscale = scale(gene_norm_PCA, center=TRUE,scale=TRUE) %*% pca_res$rotation[, 1:2]

dim(pca_mult_loadings)
pca_mult_loadings[1:5, ]
# versus

dim(pca_res$x)
pca_mult_loadings[1:5, 1:2]; pca_res$x[1:5, 1:2]


plot(pca_mult_loadings[1:50, 1], pca_res$x[1:50, 1]); abline(a=0,b=1)
plot(pca_mult_loadings_centerscale[1:50, 1], pca_res$x[1:50, 1]); abline(a=0,b=1)
```

```{r}

#| warning: false
```

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(srtdisk)

crc10 <- srtdisk::LoadH5AD(sprintf('%s/subset_adata_SCARF_10celltypes_10perturbations.h5ad', data_dir), verbose = TRUE)
crc48 <- srtdisk::LoadH5AD(sprintf('%s/subset_adata_SCARF_10celltypes_48perturbations.h5ad', data_dir), verbose = TRUE)
```
